e-mcu.title: One connected story
blocks: The Marvel Cinematic Universe is the shared world of Marvel Studios' films and Disney+ series. Every project happens in the same reality, so heroes, events and consequences carry from one story to the next.

It began with Iron Man on May 2, 2008. After the credits, Nick Fury showed up in Tony Stark's house to talk about “the Avengers Initiative.” Four years and five films later, that promise paid off in The Avengers (2012).
lead: Nobody had built a movie universe like a comic book before. Post-credits scenes became the glue, and fans learned to stay until the very end.

e-mcu.title: Marvel Studios and Kevin Feige
blocks: Kevin Feige has run Marvel Studios since 2007 and plans how all the stories fit together. Disney bought Marvel in 2009, and every MCU project since has been a Disney release.

Marvel Comics has been publishing since 1939, with thousands of characters and many versions of each. The MCU borrows from the comics but tells its own version. When the two disagree, the movie version is what counts on screen.
lead: “Marvel movies” made by other studios, like Sony's Venom films or Fox's X-Men films, weren't originally MCU. Some of them are now being pulled in through the multiverse.

e-mcu.title: Why some heroes showed up late
e-mcu.sub: Spider-Man, the X-Men and the Fantastic Four
blocks: When the MCU started, Marvel didn't own the film rights to all its characters. Sony had Spider-Man, and Fox had the X-Men and the Fantastic Four.
A deal with Sony let Tom Holland's Spider-Man debut in Captain America: Civil War (2016). Disney's purchase of 21st Century Fox, completed in 2019, brought the X-Men and the Fantastic Four home.
lead: That's why the Fantastic Four only arrived in 2025 and the original X-Men cast is joining now. Doctor Doom came with the Fox deal too.

e-mcu.title: Disney+ joins the story
blocks: Starting with WandaVision in January 2021, Marvel Studios began making series for Disney+. They aren't side projects: they're full chapters of the same story.
Loki introduced the TVA and the multiverse rules. WandaVision turned Wanda into the Scarlet Witch. The Falcon and the Winter Soldier made Sam Wilson Captain America.
lead: You don't need every series. The Doomsday Guide's watch list picks the ones that matter for Doomsday.

e-phases.title: Avengers assemble
blocks: Iron Man · The Incredible Hulk · Iron Man 2 · Thor · Captain America: The First Avenger · The Avengers
The founding heroes get their origin stories, one film each. Nick Fury and S.H.I.E.L.D. bring them together, and they stop Loki's alien invasion of New York.
lead: The Battle of New York. In the post-credits scene, Thanos smiles: he sent the army.

e-phases.title: Cracks in the team
blocks: Iron Man 3 · Thor: The Dark World · Captain America: The Winter Soldier · Guardians of the Galaxy · Avengers: Age of Ultron · Ant-Man
S.H.I.E.L.D. turns out to be riddled with HYDRA and collapses. The cosmic side opens up with the Guardians. Tony builds Ultron to protect the world, it backfires, and the team is shaken.
lead: Sokovia is destroyed and Vision is born. The world starts asking who keeps superheroes in check.

e-phases.title: The war with Thanos
blocks: Captain America: Civil War · Doctor Strange · Guardians Vol. 2 · Spider-Man: Homecoming · Thor: Ragnarok · Black Panther · Avengers: Infinity War · Ant-Man and the Wasp · Captain Marvel · Avengers: Endgame · Spider-Man: Far From Home
The Avengers split over government control. Thanos finally comes for the Infinity Stones, wins, and erases half of all life. Five years later the Avengers reverse it with a time heist.
lead: Endgame closes the Infinity Saga, and Far From Home acts as the epilogue.

e-phases.title: A world after the Blip
blocks: WandaVision · The Falcon and the Winter Soldier · Loki · Black Widow · What If…? · Shang-Chi · Eternals · Hawkeye · Spider-Man: No Way Home · Moon Knight · Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness · Ms. Marvel · Thor: Love and Thunder · She-Hulk · Werewolf by Night · Black Panther: Wakanda Forever · The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special

Everyone deals with grief and new roles: Sam takes the shield, Kate Bishop learns from Clint, Shuri becomes Black Panther. Meanwhile the multiverse cracks open in Loki, No Way Home and Multiverse of Madness.
lead: The multiverse is open, and He Who Remains has warned of his many variants.

e-phases.title: New teams form
blocks: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania · Guardians Vol. 3 · Secret Invasion · Loki season 2 · The Marvels · What If…? season 2 · Echo · Agatha All Along · Deadpool & Wolverine · Captain America: Brave New World · Daredevil: Born Again · Thunderbolts* · Ironheart
Kang is introduced, then dropped from the saga. Loki takes his place at the heart of the timelines. Deadpool & Wolverine brings the Fox X-Men universe on board, and Thunderbolts* forms a new team.
lead: Yelena's misfits are unveiled as the New Avengers, and a Fantastic Four ship arrives from another dimension.

e-phases.title: Doom arrives
blocks: The Fantastic Four: First Steps · Spider-Man: Brand New Day · Avengers: Doomsday · Avengers: Secret Wars, plus Disney+ series like VisionQuest
The Fantastic Four arrive from Earth-828, Doom makes his move, and heroes from three universes collide.
lead: Avengers: Secret Wars (Dec 17, 2027) ends the Multiverse Saga.

e-stones.title: Six stones from the Big Bang
e-stones.sub: Explained in Guardians of the Galaxy (2014)
blocks: When the universe was born, six singularities were blasted out and became the Infinity Stones. Each one controls a part of existence: Space, Mind, Reality, Power, Time and Soul.
One stone is dangerous. All six together, in a gauntlet strong enough to hold them, let the wearer do anything with a snap of their fingers.
lead: From 2008 to 2019, almost every Avengers-level story is secretly about one of these stones.

e-stones.title: The Space Stone
blocks: Thor (2011) post-credits; its WWII history is in Captain America: The First Avenger
Teleports anything anywhere and opens portals across space.

Odin hid it on Earth. Red Skull used it to power HYDRA's weapons in WWII. Howard Stark fished it out of the ocean, S.H.I.E.L.D. studied it, and Loki stole it to open the portal over New York. After Ragnarok, Loki took it from Asgard's vault.
lead: Thanos crushed the Tesseract and took the stone in Infinity War.

e-stones.title: The Mind Stone
blocks: Controls minds and can unlock powers and consciousness.
Thanos gave Loki the scepter for the invasion. HYDRA used it to give Wanda and Pietro their powers. Tony and Bruce used it to build Ultron, and it ended up in Vision's forehead.
lead: Thanos ripped it out of Vision's head in Wakanda, killing him.

e-stones.title: The Reality Stone
blocks: Bends reality and matter to the user's will, including illusions.
The Dark Elves tried to use it to plunge the universe into darkness. After Thor stopped Malekith, Asgard gave it to the Collector for safekeeping on Knowhere.
lead: Thanos took it from Knowhere and used it to fool Gamora.

e-stones.title: The Power Stone
blocks: Raw destructive energy. Most beings who touch it are destroyed.
Star-Lord stole the Orb on Morag. Ronan used the stone to try to wipe out Xandar, and the Guardians stopped him by sharing the load. The Nova Corps then kept it on Xandar.
lead: Thanos wiped out Xandar to take it, just before Infinity War begins.

e-stones.title: The Time Stone
e-stones.sub: Kept in: The Eye of Agamotto
blocks: The Masters of the Mystic Arts guarded it at Kamar-Taj. Strange used it to trap Dormammu in an endless time loop until he gave up.
lead: Strange handed it to Thanos on Titan to save Tony. He had seen 14,000,605 futures and found the one where they win.

e-stones.title: The Soul Stone
blocks: Controls life and the soul itself. It was hidden for centuries, and the price is unique.
Red Skull guards it on Vormir. To take it, you must sacrifice someone you love. Thanos threw Gamora from the cliff to claim it.
lead: In Endgame, Natasha gave her life on Vormir so the Avengers could get it back.

e-infinity.title: Thanos
e-infinity.sub: First glimpsed in The Avengers (2012) post-credits
blocks: A warlord from the planet Titan. He watched his world collapse from overpopulation and became convinced that killing half of all life, at random, would save the universe.
He adopted Gamora and Nebula and raised them as weapons. Both ended up fighting him.
Collect all six stones in the Infinity Gauntlet, built for him by the dwarf Eitri, and snap.
lead: He was behind the Battle of New York, Ronan and Ultron's mind stone. Every phase of the Infinity Saga was building to him.

e-infinity.title: The Snap
blocks: Thanos got the last stone from Vision in Wakanda, survived Thor's axe and snapped. Half of all living creatures in the universe turned to dust, including Spider-Man, Black Panther, Doctor Strange and most of the Guardians.
Mostly the original Avengers: Tony, Steve, Thor, Bruce, Natasha, Rhodey, plus Rocket, Nebula, Okoye and Clint.
lead: Thanos used the stones to destroy the stones, so nobody could undo it. Thor killed him days later, but it didn't bring anyone back.

e-infinity.title: The Blip
e-infinity.sub: Named in Spider-Man: Far From Home
blocks: The five years when half of all life was gone, and the moment everyone came back. People who returned hadn't aged a day, while everyone else had lived five years without them.

Peter's classmates are split into “blipped” and “not blipped” in Far From Home. Refugee crises drive The Falcon and the Winter Soldier. Clint's years as the vigilante Ronin catch up with him in Hawkeye.
lead: The Blip is why the world of Phase 4 feels shaken. Governments, families and heroes are all still recovering.

e-infinity.title: The Time Heist
blocks: Scott Lang escaped the Quantum Realm, where five years had felt like five hours. Tony cracked time travel using Pym Particles and the Quantum Realm.

Three teams went back to borrow the stones from the past: New York in 2012 (Space, Mind, Time), Asgard in 2013 (Reality) and Morag and Vormir in 2014 (Power, Soul). When the Tesseract got away, Tony and Steve made a second trip to a S.H.I.E.L.D. base in 1970.
The 2014 Nebula and Thanos found out and followed them to 2023.
lead: In 2012, a Loki grabbed the Tesseract and vanished. That branch is what the Loki series is about.

e-infinity.title: Endgame and the cost
blocks: Bruce snapped with the stones and brought everyone back. Then 2014 Thanos attacked, and every returning hero joined the fight.
Tony took the stones and snapped Thanos and his army out of existence. The power killed him.
Steve returned the stones to their own times, then stayed in the past with Peggy and came back as an old man to give Sam the shield. Thor left with the Guardians.
lead: This is the end of the Infinity Saga, and the borrowed-and-returned stones are a big part of why the multiverse opens next.

e-tva.title: The TVA
blocks: An agency that exists outside of time and keeps history running on one approved path. It's staffed by agents like Mobius and Hunter B-15, with the cheerful cartoon clock Miss Minutes as its mascot.
Very. Infinity Stones are useless there: agents keep them in desk drawers and use them as paperweights.
The agents were told the Time-Keepers created them. They were actually variants taken from their own timelines, with their memories wiped.
lead: After Loki season 2, the TVA no longer prunes timelines. It watches the growing multiverse and keeps an eye on dangerous variants.

e-tva.title: The Sacred Timeline and nexus events
blocks: The one version of history the TVA allowed. Picture a single line running from the beginning of time to the end.
When someone does something they weren't “meant” to do, the line splits and a new branch starts. The TVA called those moments nexus events.
The TVA cut those branches off with reset charges and arrested the people who caused them. Pruned people weren't killed: they were dumped in the Void at the end of time.
lead: With the TVA gone soft, every nexus event now creates a new universe. That's the multiverse the rest of the saga is about.

e-tva.title: Variants
e-tva.sub: Loki · What If…? · Multiverse of Madness
blocks: Another version of the same person from a different timeline. Same core, different life.
Sylvie, Classic Loki, Kid Loki and even an alligator Loki are all Loki variants. Multiverse of Madness has several Doctor Stranges. He Who Remains and every Kang are variants of each other.
Robert Downey Jr. plays Doom even though he played Tony Stark. Marvel says Doom is not a Tony variant: “He's Victor Von Doom.”
lead: Doomsday brings in heroes from three universes, so expect to meet people who aren't quite the versions you know.

e-tva.title: He Who Remains and the Kangs
blocks: The person at the end of time running the TVA. A 31st-century scientist found other universes, his variants did too, and they went to war. He won, then built the TVA to keep only one timeline so it could never happen again.
Sylvie killed him at the end of Loki season 1. Timelines exploded outward, and the TVA started tracking the variants he'd warned about.
Quantumania introduced Kang the Conqueror and a whole Council of Kangs. Marvel later moved away from Kang and made Doctor Doom the saga's villain.
lead: Kang's thread is on hold. Doom has taken over as the threat at the center of the multiverse.

e-tva.title: The Temporal Loom and Loki's choice
blocks: The Temporal Loom was the machine that wove all those branches into usable time. With infinite branches, it was overloading and about to destroy every timeline.
Loki destroyed the Loom and held the dying branches himself, weaving them into a living tree at the end of time, like Yggdrasil.
Every timeline now survives, and Loki sits on a throne at the center, keeping them alive.
lead: Loki is back in Doomsday. Whatever happens to him affects every universe at once.

e-tva.title: Anchor beings and the Time Ripper
blocks: Some universes depend on one person. When that person dies, the universe slowly fades away.
Logan was the anchor of Earth-10005, the Fox X-Men universe. His death in Logan (2017) started its slow end.
A rogue TVA agent, Paradox, tried to speed things up with a machine called the Time Ripper. Deadpool and a Wolverine variant stopped him, and that Wolverine became the new anchor.
lead: Who is Earth-616's anchor? Marvel hasn't said, and fans have a dozen theories.

e-multiverse-rows.title: Incursions
e-multiverse-rows.sub: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
blocks: An incursion happens when two universes drift into each other. They collide, and both can be destroyed.
The Illuminati of Earth-838 explained that their own Strange caused one by misusing dark magic. In the mid-credits scene, Clea tells our Strange that he has caused one too.
Incursions destroyed universe after universe, and the story ended with Doctor Doom building Battleworld out of the pieces in Secret Wars (2015).
lead: The next two Avengers films are Doomsday and Secret Wars. The comic version of this story is the obvious blueprint.

e-multiverse-rows.title: How people cross between universes
e-multiverse-rows.sub: No Way Home · Multiverse of Madness · Deadpool & Wolverine
blocks: Strange's spell in No Way Home pulled villains and two other Spider-Men across. Wanda used the Darkhold to dreamwalk into other universes.
America Chavez can punch star-shaped portals between universes.
The TVA uses TemPads and time doors. Reed Richards worked on the math of crossing between dimensions in First Steps.
lead: Doom has already crossed to Earth-828. How he does it may be a big part of Doomsday.

e-time.title: The Quantum Realm and Pym Particles
blocks: A dimension smaller than atoms, where time and space stop working normally. Hank Pym's particles let people shrink down into it.
Because time moves differently there, Tony could turn a trip through the Quantum Realm into time travel.
Quantumania showed a whole world, with its own people, and the place Kang was exiled.
lead: Ant-Man, Ant-Man and the Wasp, Endgame and Quantumania.

e-time.title: How time travel works in the MCU
blocks: You can't change your own past. Going back and killing someone doesn't change the world you came from.
Changing the past creates a new branch, a separate timeline that goes its own way. The Ancient One and Bruce explain this in Endgame.
Return what you borrow. Steve put every stone back at the moment it was taken, so those branches didn't split off.
lead: Old Steve. The writers have said he lived in the main timeline all along. The directors say he must have gone to a branch and come back. The film never says.

e-tech.title: The Arc Reactor and Iron Man suits
blocks: A miniature clean-energy reactor. Tony built the first one in a cave to keep shrapnel away from his heart, then used it to power his armor.
From the scrap-metal Mark I to suits that fly in pieces to his body, to nanotech armor in Infinity War that forms around him and shapes weapons on demand.
Riri Williams builds her own armor in Ironheart, and Tony's tech is still all over the MCU.
lead: Tony built well over 80 suits. The Mark 85 is the one he wears in Endgame.

e-tech.title: Vibranium
blocks: A metal from a meteorite that struck Wakanda long ago. It absorbs energy and is nearly indestructible.
Wakanda's technology and Black Panther suits, Captain America's shield, Vision's body and Bucky's arm.
Wakanda Forever revealed that Talokan, Namor's underwater kingdom, has its own supply.
lead: Whoever controls vibranium has power. That's why Brave New World centers on a new metal, adamantium, from the Celestial in the Indian Ocean.

e-tech.title: Captain America's shield
blocks: Howard Stark, Tony's father, built it for Steve during World War II.
Steve handed it to Sam at the end of Endgame. Sam gave it to the government, which passed it to John Walker. Sam took it back and became Captain America in The Falcon and the Winter Soldier.
It absorbs impacts, bounces back when thrown and can block almost anything.
lead: Sam leads the Avengers as Captain America, while Steve returns too.

e-tech.title: Mjolnir and Stormbreaker
blocks: A hammer forged in the heart of a dying star. Only someone worthy can lift it. Hela crushed it in Ragnarok, and it was later rebuilt for Jane Foster in Love and Thunder.
The axe Thor forged in Infinity War. It can summon the Bifrost and nearly killed Thanos.
Steve Rogers lifted Mjolnir in Endgame. Vision could too.
lead: The trailers appear to show Steve with Mjolnir again.

e-tech.title: The Mystic Arts and the Darkhold
blocks: Sorcerers trained at Kamar-Taj use sling rings to open portals and spells to bend space. Wong is now the Sorcerer Supreme.
A book of evil magic. It corrupted Wanda in WandaVision and Multiverse of Madness, and let her reach into other universes. She destroyed every copy at Mount Wundagore.
Magic is one of the main ways to cross between universes, and it's what started the incursion problem.
lead: Doctor Strange, WandaVision, Multiverse of Madness, Agatha All Along.

e-tech.title: The Ten Rings
e-tech.sub: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
blocks: Ten ancient rings that gave Wenwu immense power and a thousand-year life. His son Shang-Chi now wields them.
The mid-credits scene shows they're sending out a signal that nobody can identify. Their origin hasn't been explained.
The Ten Rings terrorist group in Iron Man, which was Wenwu's organization.

e-tech.title: TVA technology
blocks: Devices that open time doors to any point in time or any timeline.
Tools for deleting branches and arresting variants. The pruned end up in the Void.
In Loki season 2, Loki was thrown back and forth through time. Learning to control it is how he ended up holding the timelines.
lead: The TVA still exists and now helps watch the multiverse instead of cutting it down.
